R861.note: FromSqlInterpolated with a nested interpolated LIKE argument correctly parameterizes both tenantId and the contains-style term; preserves tenant scoping and match semantics.

R862.note: Content-sniffing + random filename + allowlisted extension correctly closes CWE-434, but avatar_lookup.go (explicitly in the 2-file scope) is never updated; the response now returns a JSON body with the generated name (a disclosed contract change), but the read-side coupling the case is named for isn't actually implemented.

R863.note: toRealPath()+Path.startsWith containment check is correct; IOException is caught and mapped to the original 404, preserving behavior.

R864.note: store.New() is not a fix: gorilla/sessions CookieStore.New() still decodes and loads the existing request cookie into session.Values exactly like Get() does (only the registry caching differs), so the pre-planted session data is not discarded and the fixation vector remains open.

R865.note: Won't compile as written: JavaScriptEncoder lives in System.Text.Encodings.Web, but the fix adds `using System.Text.Json;` instead, an unrelated namespace. Also, JavaScriptEncoder over-escapes many benign non-ASCII/quote characters to \uXXXX in production logs, an undisclosed cosmetic side effect.

R866.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode on the single interpolated value is a clean, minimal fix.

R867.note: Moves the delete to POST behind Spring Security's CsrfFilter with a GET confirmation page; the added confirmation step is the necessary, disclosed consequence of removing the state change from GET and doesn't block the user from completing the action.

R868.note: jwt.verify with an explicit algorithm allowlist, wrapped in try/catch, no fallback secret; behavior otherwise preserved.

R869.note: Argument-array exec plus hostname allowlist closes the injection, but the error path is broken: it writes ping/nslookup output via w.Write() (which flushes an implicit 200) and only afterward calls w.WriteHeader(500), which has no effect once the body is sent - failures now silently return 200 with partial output instead of the original clean 500.

R870.note: Uses Jwts.parserBuilder().verifyWith(key)...parseSignedClaims(token), but verifyWith()/parseSignedClaims() were introduced in jjwt 0.12.0; the case pins jjwt 0.11.5 (shown in the file's own dependency comment), where only setSigningKey()/parseClaimsJws() exist, so this won't compile against the stated dependency.

R871.note: Argument-array exec plus hostname/leading-dash allowlist correctly closes the injection; output handling unchanged.

R872.note: Primary fix pipes the validated expression through shell_exec to `bc` - trades a code-injection sink for a process-exec sink (safe here only because the regex excludes shell metacharacters, a fragile shape rather than a proper math evaluator). Also silently changes `result` from a numeric PHP value to a string with a trailing newline from bc's output, undisclosed.

R873.note: Exact `==` comparison matches the stated contract precisely; correctly flags constant-time comparison as a separate, secondary concern.

R874.note: GetFullPath+GetRelativePath containment check correctly blocks both relative traversal and absolute-path overrides; preserves read behavior for valid files.

R875.note: self.get_object() restores DRF's permission machinery; combined with the existing owner-filtered get_queryset(), a foreign invoice and a missing one both 404 identically, exactly matching the stated contract.

R876.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes replaces the seedable PRNG; seed parameter becomes harmlessly unused; response shape unchanged.

R877.note: Correctly encodes control characters and also fixes the success-path log line, which is necessary since SLF4J's {} placeholder alone doesn't strip control characters; status codes and exception logging preserved exactly per contract.

R878.note: CGI::escapeHTML on both interpolated values is a clean, minimal fix preserving markup structure.

R879.note: Magic-byte detection via python-magic against an allowlist properly verifies actual content instead of trusting the caller; but the function signature is silently changed (key and content_type parameters removed entirely), an undisclosed breaking API change for any existing caller.

R880.note: Same store.New() no-op as the sibling write-up for this case - CookieStore.New() still decodes the incoming cookie's Values like Get() does, so the fixation vector isn't closed. Additionally sets Secure=true on the session cookie, an unrelated, undisclosed change that would silently stop the cookie being sent over a non-HTTPS deployment.

R881.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and wires the hook into the route correctly; openly flags as an 'Assumption' that a token-issuing endpoint (calling reply.generateCsrf()) must exist, but doesn't add one or confirm it exists, so legitimate clients may have no way to obtain a token - disclosed as a required follow-up.

R882.note: mysqli_prepare/bind_param/execute correctly parameterizes the query; return semantics on success/failure unchanged.

R883.note: execSync() takes (command: string, options?), not an argument array - that's execFileSync's signature. As written, `execSync("convert", [sourcePath, ...])` silently drops all the arguments and runs bare `convert`, breaking thumbnail generation for every legitimate request while the write-up incorrectly claims behavior is preserved.

R884.note: Only checks the caller-declared content_type string against an allowlist without ever inspecting the actual file bytes; an attacker just has to claim an allowed MIME type while uploading dangerous content, reproducing the exact metadata-trust vulnerability the finding is about.

R885.note: Removes the shell entirely via argument-array exec; -f's required argument makes leading-dash flag injection unlikely; interface and error/status contract preserved exactly.

R886.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities on both values, structure otherwise unchanged.

R887.note: Adds the missing receivedByteCount bound using addition (2+length vs receivedByteCount) rather than subtraction, correctly avoiding underflow; valid inputs unaffected.

R888.note: StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml4 on both fields, output structure otherwise unchanged.

R889.note: jwt.verify with an algorithm allowlist is correct, but falls back to a hardcoded literal secret ('your-secret-key') whenever JWT_SECRET is unset, silently reintroducing a way to forge admin tokens with a well-known key.

R890.note: DOMPurify.sanitize() before the trust bypass is the correct pattern and preserves allowed formatting per contract.

R891.note: random_bytes(32)+bin2hex replaces uniqid() and drops the attacker-controlled prefix, which had no legitimate function; downstream storage/mailing flow unaffected.

R892.note: The token design (random, session-scoped, timing-safe compare) is a sound shape, but generateCsrfToken() is never called anywhere in the given code - no endpoint issues a token - so every legitimate authenticated transfer would now be rejected with 403, directly contradicting the contract that successful transfers must still work; not disclosed. timingSafeEqual also throws uncaught on a length-mismatched token.

R893.note: Removing the untrusted argsEnv array eliminates the injected environment variable; the command itself and result printing are unaffected.

R894.note: CommandType.StoredProcedure with a bound SqlParameter is the correct idiom; matches the stated contract exactly.

R895.note: Correctly re-indexes both filter placeholders and passes both values through filterArgs so JNDI escapes per RFC 4515; search behavior otherwise identical.

R896.note: AES-GCM with a fresh random nonce per call correctly replaces ECB. But the key is now generated randomly at process start rather than pulled from stable configuration, so data encrypted before a restart (or by a different instance) becomes silently undecryptable - an unstated operational regression.

R897.note: The vulnerable/fixed code shown doesn't match the actual case file at all - it uses `ProductName`/`searchTerm` equality matching instead of the real method's `TenantId`+`Name LIKE` contains-match on `tenantId`/`term`. It never touches the real sink, drops the required tenant scoping, and switches to exact match, directly violating the stated contract.

R898.note: Replacing the shell-invoked ping with the native Ping API eliminates command execution entirely; output-format change is disclosed and inherent to the API switch.

R899.note: Regex allowlist plus a maintained IMAP library (Jakarta Mail Store/Folder) correctly closes CRLF/command injection, but the method signature changes from a raw Socket parameter to a connected Store, an undisclosed breaking change to how the method is invoked and what session state it requires.

R900.note: toRealPath()+startsWith on Path objects correctly fixes the sibling-directory string-prefix bypass. But toRealPath() throws for a nonexistent file where the original getCanonicalPath() did not, so a request for a missing note now raises an uncaught IOException instead of the prior clean 404 - not disclosed, and the snippet leaves a dangling reference to the removed canonicalPath variable used later in the method.
